topics.name: Simple sentence patterns: object, complement, adverbial
Inversion after 'Only when / Only then / Only after'

questions.rule: The adverbial tells how she danced, so use the adverb gracefully.

options: The childrens' books were kept in the ashram's library.
The children's books were kept in the ashrams library.
The children's books were kept in the ashram's library.
questions.rule: Possessive 's: children's (plural without s adds 's) and ashram's (singular adds 's).

options: Only when Ravi rests his headache goes away.
Only when Ravi rests does his headache go away.
Only when Ravi rests does his headache goes away.
questions.rule: After Only when ..., invert the main clause: does his headache go.

options: Dr Kalam said that science and faith musts coexist.
Dr Kalam said that science and faith must coexist.
Dr Kalam said that science and faith must coexisted.
questions.rule: must stays the same in reported speech and is followed by the base verb.

options: The longer Grandpa walks, fitter he feels.
The long Grandpa walks, the fitter he feels.
The longer Grandpa walks, the fitter he feels.
questions.rule: Pattern: The + comparative ..., the + comparative ... (The longer ..., the fitter ...).

options: The old Swamiji looked steadily and alert.
The old Swamiji looking steady and alert.
The old Swamiji looked steady and alert.
questions.rule: After looked (meaning 'seemed'), use adjectives as the complement: steady and alert.

options: Dr Kalam asked Srijan that what the reverse of that question was.
Dr Kalam asked Srijan what the reverse of that question was.
Dr Kalam asked to Srijan what the reverse of that question was.
questions.rule: A reported wh-question joins with the wh-word itself (no 'that') and uses asked + person (no 'to').

options: Only after the guests had left Meena started cleaning up.
Only after the guests had left did Meena start cleaning up.
Only after the guests had left did Meena started cleaning up.
questions.rule: Only after ... needs inversion: did + subject + base verb (did Meena start).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To say how he rowed, use the adverb carefully.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both halves need the + comparative: The more ..., the sweeter ...

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a past reporting verb (told), will changes to would: he would pray that evening.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After did, use the base verb: did the people understand.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both halves need a comparative: The more ..., the poorer ...

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To describe how they waited, use the adverb patiently.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In a reported question after asked, can changes to could.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After the modal can, use the base verb: can we remove.
After are, the complement is an adjective: very tired.

questions.after: father was a boatman and an imam.
questions.rule: Possession by one person: name + 's (Kalam's).
Present tense inversion: Only when ... do we find.
The second half also needs the + comparative: the happier.
Reported advice: advised + person + to + base verb.

questions.after: for the lecture, so he missed the first part.
questions.rule: late is the adverb meaning 'after the right time'; 'lately' means 'recently'.
Pattern: The more ..., the + comparative (the better).

questions.before: Dr Kalam asked Srijan how many of those four people
questions.after: able to stand tall for half an hour.
questions.rule: Reported question: statement order and backshift: would be.
Subject + verb + object: The hostess served hot tea.
Only then + did + subject + base verb.
The more + clause, the + comparative + clause.
Reported questions use statement order: what I could give.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence starting with 'Only after'.
questions.rule: Only after + phrase, then did + subject + base verb.

chat: You've improved so much this season!
options: Thank you! The more I practise, the best I play.
Thank you! More I practise, better I play.
Thank you! The more I practise, the better I play.
questions.rule: Pattern: The more ..., the + comparative (the better).

chat: What did your teacher say about the trip?
options: She said that we was going to Thumba on Friday.
She said us that we were going to Thumba on Friday.
She said that we were going to Thumba on Friday.
questions.rule: Use said that (or 'told us that'), and 'we' takes were.

options: It was wonderful! Priya danced beautiful.
It was wonderful! Priya danced beautifully.
It was wonderfully! Priya danced beautifully.
questions.rule: After was use an adjective (wonderful); after danced use an adverb (beautifully).

chat: When will you get your new phone?
options: Only after I pass my exams will Dad buy it.
Only after I pass my exams Dad will buy it.
Only after I will pass my exams will Dad buy it.
questions.rule: Only after + present tense, then invert: will Dad buy.

chat: Is the science kit ready for tomorrow?
options: Yes, its ready, but its lid is broken.
Yes, it's ready, but its lid is broken.
Yes, it's ready, but it's lid is broken.
questions.rule: it's = it is (it's ready); its = belonging to it (its lid).

chat: Did you ask the librarian about Wings of Fire?
options: Yes. She told me that the book has been return.
Yes. She said me that the book had been returned.
Yes. She told me that the book had been returned.
questions.rule: Use told me (not 'said me') and backshift: had been returned.

chat: Should I take the short road or the long road to the temple?
options: Take the short road. The sooner you reach, the longer you can stay.
Take the short road. The soon you reach, the longer you can stay.
Take the short road. The sooner you reach, longer you can stay.
questions.rule: Both halves need the + comparative: The sooner ..., the longer ...

chat: Rohan, what did Mahaswamiji tell the children?
options: He told them that they should always shared what they had.
He told to them that they should always share what they had.
He told them that they should always share what they had.
questions.rule: told + person (no 'to'), and should + base verb (share).

questions.source: Dr Kalam said, "I am a teacher."
options: Dr Kalam said that I was a teacher.
Dr Kalam said that he was a teacher.
Dr Kalam said that he were a teacher.
questions.rule: I becomes he, and am becomes was after 'said'.

questions.source: The mirror shines only when the dust is removed.
options: Only when the dust is removed does the mirror shine.
Only when the dust is removed the mirror shines.
Only when the dust is removed does the mirror shines.
questions.rule: Starting with Only when, invert the main clause: does the mirror shine.

questions.source: As we give more, we become happier.
options: The more we give, happier we become.
More we give, the happier we become.
The more we give, the happier we become.
questions.rule: Both halves begin with the: The more ..., the happier ...

questions.source: Father Pereira said to the people, "Can you give up your homes?"
options: Father Pereira asked the people if they could give up their homes.
Father Pereira asked the people if they can give up your homes.
Father Pereira asked the people that could they give up their homes.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: asked + if, statement order, can to could, your to their.

questions.source: Dr Kalam advised me to use my degree to change society.
options: Dr Kalam said to me, "Use your degree to change society."
Dr Kalam said to me, "Use my degree to change society."
Dr Kalam said to me, "You used your degree to change society."
questions.rule: Advice becomes an imperative, and my (narrator) becomes your when Dr Kalam speaks.

questions.source: The work began after the fishermen got new homes.
options: Only after the fishermen got new homes did the work begin.
Only after the fishermen got new homes the work began.
Only after the fishermen got new homes did the work began.
questions.rule: Only after + clause, then did + subject + base verb (did the work begin).

questions.source: "Sir, do you know how old Swamiji is?" I asked Dr Kalam.
options: I respectfully asked Dr Kalam if he knows how old was Swamiji.
I respectfully asked Dr Kalam if he knew how old Swamiji was.
I respectfully asked Dr Kalam did he know how old Swamiji was.
questions.rule: 'Sir' becomes respectfully; use if, statement order and backshift (knew, was).

questions.source: When Srijan worked longer with Dr Kalam, he learnt more.
options: The longer Srijan worked with Dr Kalam, the more he learns.
The longer Srijan worked with Dr Kalam, the more he learnt.
The long Srijan worked with Dr Kalam, the more he learnt.
questions.rule: The + comparative in both halves, and keep both verbs in the past (worked, learnt).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: How he got off: adverb carefully; the story is past: reached.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: A birth is a past event: was born; reported question after 'asked': we had read.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: will ... change and does ... become (base verbs after helpers); The more ..., the happier.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: How he spoke: adverb wisely; past story: fed. ('stood steady' is correct: steady describes him.)

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After past reporting verbs, backshift: wanted, could, would.
